audit.title: Transient early reionization allows for a high optical depth while remaining consistent with kSZ measurements
audit.read_status: Full main text, relevant supplemental methods/robustness and independently retrieved historical papers read.
audit.summary:
Bansal, Kern and Huterer test whether an early ionization episode could raise CMB optical depth without violating late reionization constraints. Their modified 21cmFAST simulations couple hypothetical supermassive Population III.1 sources to recombination and radiative feedback. A fiducial flash near $z=23$ raises $\tau$ from 0.060 to 0.096 while barely changing reionization's endpoint. Small, weakly clustered relic bubbles shift their kinetic Sunyaev–Zel'dovich power to much smaller angular scales: at $\ell=3000$, the patchy signal increases from 1.64 to 2.13 $\mu\mathrm{K}^2$. This lies below three of four SPT-3G foreground-dependent upper limits, but exceeds the tightest 1.8 $\mu\mathrm{K}^2$ limit.

A Fisher forecast combining Simons Observatory spectra and lensing, multiple kSZ bands, Ly$\alpha$ constraints and UV luminosity-function priors reaches $\sigma[\tau(z>12)]=0.0077$. Anchoring late ionization is essential; kSZ plus the forest alone reaches 0.015. These are conditional forecasts, not evidence for a flash or dark stars. Linear-velocity modeling omits non-Gaussian momentum terms, and the high-multipole spectrum is less numerically robust. Compatibility with selected kSZ limits also does not establish compatibility with the full Planck polarization likelihood.
cautions: Conclusions say no tension with any current pkSZ limits, but results explicitly exceed tightest 1.8 microK^2 foreground scenario. Use qualified statement.
SO forecast incorporates small-scale spectra/lensing optical-depth information; do not call 0.008 a kSZ-only constraint.

Main text says previous Aggarwal model relics neither recombine nor interact. Independently read Aggarwal PDF: it DOES prescribe uniform recombination with frozen morphology. Say new work couples recombination/feedback self-consistently, not first inclusion of recombination.
Fiducial total tau0.096 here versus0.097 companion; preserve each value or round≈0.10 when grouping.
Authors explicitly do not establish feasibility of dark-star formation.

audit.title: A flash before dawn: 21 cm signatures of transient reionization from supermassive Pop III stars
audit.publication_status: Submitted to PRD, according to arXiv comments
audit.read_status: Full main text including forecast assumptions, Table2 and model-dependence discussion read.
audit.summary:
The companion paper develops the shared simulation: hypothetical stars grow during a dark-matter-supported phase, ignite, leave ionized relic regions, and produce black holes whose later X-rays heat the intergalactic gas. Isolation, Lyman–Werner feedback and recombination regulate this sequence. Its distinctive 21-cm predictions are earlier absorption from Lyman-$\alpha$ coupling and enhanced fluctuations from hot relic bubbles against cold surrounding gas.

For 1,080 hours with SKA-Low's assumed AA4 configuration, an 18-parameter Fisher forecast gives $\sigma_\tau=0.0129$–0.0166 across optimistic-to-conservative foreground cuts. Adding a hypothetical 40–90 MHz global-signal experiment improves a moderately optimistic case to 0.0121 around the deliberately chosen $\tau=0.097$ model. That additional experiment requires foreground residuals at roughly the tens-of-millikelvin level and coverage extending below existing plans. The quoted very large signal-detection significances compare fixed models without marginalizing standard galaxy parameters; they are not discovery significances. At these redshifts, 21-cm power mainly traces spin-temperature fluctuations, making its conversion to ionization and optical depth model dependent. The pair therefore identifies complementary observational tests of an assumed early episode, rather than demonstrating a resolution of DESI–CMB tensions.

audit.title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
audit.read_status: Full main text and appendices read; primary JUNO and Borexino inputs independently checked.
audit.summary:
Leyton and Dye combine KamLAND, Borexino, SNO+ and JUNO geoneutrino rates with site-specific lithosphere predictions. A common mantle signal fits acceptably ($\chi^2=3.78$ for three degrees of freedom; $p=0.286$), giving $14.8\pm4.5$ neutrino-interaction units and $18.5\pm5.6$ TW of mantle radiogenic heating, conditional on Th/U=3.77 and K/U=13,000. The approximately $3.2\sigma$ result concerns a nonzero mantle contribution, not spatial heterogeneity.

After lithosphere subtraction, Jiangmen exceeds Kamioka by $24.6\pm13.8$ interaction units: only $1.8\sigma$, with this contrast selected after inspecting the data. The authors test nearly one million configurations across seismic anomalies, deep mantle provinces, slabs, lithosphere rescaling and local prescriptions. Plausible large-scale structures produce only small contrasts because the two detectors sample overlapping mantle volumes; reproducing the central difference requires an explicitly local contribution or offset. This is a useful diagnostic for improved JUNO exposure and local crust modeling, not evidence for a radioactive mantle anomaly. Its limitations include four nondirectional integrated rates, approximate reservoir geometry and composition, and geological priors; the inferred size of deep mantle provinces is driven almost entirely by the tomography prior.
audit.history: [Šrámek et al. (2013)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.epsl.2012.11.001) predicted geographically varying geoneutrino signals from compositionally enriched mantle structures. [Borexino's 2020 analysis](https://borex.lngs.infn.it/papers/articles/comprehensive-geoneutrino-analysis-with-borexino/) demonstrated how local-crust subtraction constrains mantle radioactivity. The new paper extends that logic to four sites. Its JUNO input, $73\pm11$ TNU, is independently reported in the [September 2026 JUNO analysis](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.37895v1), based on 207.2 live days with the geoneutrino rate free and Th/U constrained. A TNU is one inverse-beta event per year per $10^{32}$ free protons; the paper calls the equivalent unit NIU.
